title: Why Did T. Rex Have Such Tiny Arms?
description:
T. rex was a giant dinosaur. But its arms were super tiny! Why? Milo the bluebird finds out! 🐾
A fun animal fact Short for kids ages 3–8 from The Animated Zoo.

T. rex's arms were so short, they couldn't even reach its mouth! Scientists are still finding out what those little arms were for. It's a dino mystery! But T. rex had a super nose. Scientists think it could smell things far, far away.

title: Butterflies Taste With Their FEET!
description:
You taste with your tongue. A butterfly tastes with its feet! Really? Milo the bluebird finds out! 🐾
A fun animal fact Short for kids ages 3–8 from The Animated Zoo.

Yes! Butterflies have tiny tasters on their feet. When a butterfly lands on a leaf, its feet tell it if the leaf is good. And every butterfly starts out as a little caterpillar!

title: T. Rex Never Met Stegosaurus! Here's Why
description:
T. rex and Stegosaurus never met. Not even once! How come? Milo the bluebird finds out! 🐾
A fun animal fact Short for kids ages 3–8 from The Animated Zoo.

Stegosaurus lived about 150 million years ago. T. rex came much, much later. So T. rex actually lived closer in time to us than to Stegosaurus! Wow! Stegosaurus had big plates on its back, and a spiky tail called a thagomizer!

title: Dinosaurs for Kids! 5 Dino Surprises with Milo
description:
Join Milo the bluebird for a 5-minute dinosaur adventure! Meet the T. rex, Triceratops, Stegosaurus, Brachiosaurus and Pteranodon, and learn a surprise fact about each one. 🐾
Made for curious kids ages 3–8: guess-who clues, move-along fun, and a recap at the end.

What we learn today:
• T. rex had tiny arms.
• Triceratops had three horns.
• Stegosaurus had a spiky tail called a thagomizer.
• Brachiosaurus was taller than a house.
• And Pteranodon was a flying reptile, not a dinosaur!

Our zoo rule: be kind to every animal. 💙

title: Honeybees DANCE to Talk to Friends!
description:
How do bees tell their friends where the best flowers are? They dance! Milo the bluebird finds out! 🐾
A fun animal fact Short for kids ages 3–8 from The Animated Zoo.

A honeybee does a wiggly dance called the waggle dance. The dance shows the other bees which way to fly to find the flowers. And bees have five eyes! Two big ones, and three tiny ones on top.

title: Brachiosaurus Was Taller Than a House!
description:
Can you reach the top of a tree? Brachiosaurus could! How? Milo the bluebird finds out! 🐾

Brachiosaurus had a super long neck, and it was taller than a house! Its front legs were longer than its back legs, like a giraffe. It stretched up high to munch leaves at the very top of the trees.

title: Where Are a Snail's Eyes? Look Up!
description:
Your eyes are on your face. Where are a snail's eyes? Look up! Milo the bluebird finds out! 🐾

title: Pteranodon Was NOT a Dinosaur!
description:
It flew with giant wings in dinosaur times. But it was not a dinosaur! What was it? Milo the bluebird finds out! 🐾
A fun animal fact Short for kids ages 3–8 from The Animated Zoo.

This is Pteranodon. It was a flying reptile called a pterosaur. Its wings were wider than a car! It soared high over the sea. Its name means toothless wing, because it had no teeth at all!

title: Ants Can Carry Things Heavier Than Themselves!
description:

Ants are tiny, but they are super strong! An ant can lift a leaf or a crumb that is heavier than itself. And ants talk to each other with smells, and by touching their antennae.
